ceiling_statement: For any feasible system under H1-H8, institutional/reflective memory can guarantee at most: (a) provenance-complete capture - every certified state transition (H6) is committed as an episode carrying content digests of all inputs that decided it, so each remembered decision is offline-replayable (H5); (b) tamper-evidence by full recomputation - an offline verifier holding only the log bytes recomputes the whole hash chain from canonical episode bodies and detects any mutation, deletion, insertion, or reorder of any committed episode, up to hash collision-resistance (H8: recompute-and-compare, never trust the declared head); (c) rollback/fork detection exactly relative to the verifier's freshest previously-held committed checkpoint (prefix-consistency against any held prior head) - the fork-consistency bound; (d) recall as a pure deterministic function of the committed prefix, with typed UNKNOWN for anything never committed (H2). No feasible system can exceed (c) without a live external witness quorum, can remember what was not committed at event time, or can attest its own live in-RAM state (only its committed prefix).
derivation: Three independent limits. (1) Information-theoretic no-retrodiction: memory at time t is a function of bytes committed by t; an uncommitted observation is absent from every later verification, so provenance-complete capture at commit time is the maximum, and H2 forces UNKNOWN rather than reconstruction for gaps. (2) Fork-consistency bound (Mazieres-Shasha / SUNDR): with an untrusted producer and a verifier whose only input is the log bytes (H8 zero producer trust), two distinct well-formed histories are indistinguishable - internal consistency is verifiable but 'this is THE history' is not; the only escapes are a verifier-held prior checkpoint (yielding prefix-consistency relative to that floor) or an external witness quorum, which is a deployment resource B0 honestly declares NIL (authority-v2/log/witness-policy.sexp: external_quorum_status = disabled). Hence checkpoint-relative rollback detection is the hard ceiling for a single-organization deployment. (3) Self-verification limit: a process cannot produce a producer-trust-free proof of its own current runtime state (any such proof is produced by the state being attested); under H8 only the committed, externally recomputable prefix is verifiable, so 'reflective memory' maxes out at reflection over the committed chain, not over live RAM. Within these bounds, single-writer serialization (H4) plus hash chaining with the chain discipline sealed inside the hashed body attains every guarantee the limits permit - so the ceiling is attained, not merely approached.
attainment_mechanism: B0 already holds most of the seat. Keep: source/memory.lisp [RATCHET-3] append-only SHA-256 episode chain with :hv 2 sealed INSIDE the hashed body (downgrade-resistant) and full-recompute verification that trusts nothing declared; source/adoption-decision.lisp durable governed ledger with require-durable! read-back; systems/orchestrator-ai-core/provenance-model.lisp narrative chain. To reach the ceiling with SBCL + ironclad (SHA-256, Ed25519) + OS only: (1) fold the mutable, wall-clock-stamped meta registries (systems/orchestrator-meta/registry.lisp) into the same certified append-only chain - one seat per concept (H4), eliminating the mutable-registry error class structurally; (2) make chain verification continuous and fail-closed (H3): every append and every read of institutional memory re-verifies the head by recomputation, refusing on mismatch, instead of on-demand audit; (3) emit an Ed25519-signed memory checkpoint (head hash + episode count) into each release spine (machinery exists in source/authority-proof-bundle.lisp and systems/orchestrator-epistemic/release-spine.lisp), so any third party holding ANY prior release detects rollback/fork past that floor - the maximum the fork-consistency bound permits; (4) require each episode to embed the digests of all decision inputs, making replay (H5) a pure function of the chain. All constructible today; no new dependencies.
b0_gap: Per the B0 map (AX-07 row): the episode chain lives in runtime/gitignored instance state and is verified only on demand, not continuously; the meta registries (systems/orchestrator-meta/registry.lisp) are mutable and non-deterministic (:system time) - the weakest tier, outside the chain; no signed memory checkpoint is bound into the release spine, so third-party rollback detection has no structural floor; the external witness tier is honestly NIL (authority-v2/log/witness-policy.sexp), which is at-ceiling for declared resources but leaves the spec'd cosigning wire format unrealized. The chain, downgrade resistance, and recompute verification themselves are already at ceiling grade in source/memory.lisp.
lean_obligation: In Lean 4, with H : ByteString -> Digest and hypothesis (hcr : CollisionResistant H): define Episode, canon : Episode -> ByteString (injective on well-formed episodes), and chainHead : List Episode -> Digest by chainHead [] = h0, chainHead (es ++ [e]) = H (canon e ++ chainHead es). Prove: (T1 integrity) forall es es', chainHead es = chainHead es' -> es = es' (up to a collision witness contradicting hcr) - hence any mutation/deletion/insertion/reorder changes the head; (T2 checkpoint prefix) forall c1 c2, verify c1 -> verify c2 -> headAt c2 c1.length = chainHead c1 -> c1 <+: c2 (rollback detection relative to a held floor); (T3 ceiling tightness) exhibit es1 <> es2 with wellFormed es1, wellFormed es2 and no shared checkpoint, such that every verifier V : ByteString -> Bool satisfies V (serialize es1) = V (serialize es2) is not contradicted by chain verification alone - i.e., the internal-consistency predicate holds of both, formalizing that fork detection strictly requires an external floor; (T4 replay) recall q es is a total pure function returning some value or UNKNOWN, with (recall q es = value v) -> derivable v es (no output outside the committed prefix).
